title: Bicomplex maps preserve the finite first-degree image-sum filtration
statement: Let C be abelian [def-sp-abelian], K and L be Z×Z bicomplexes with total complexes [def-sp-double-complex-total], and φ:K→L a bicomplex map. Define their finite first filtrations [def-sp-filtration] by the images of inclusions over r≤p≤n in total degree n. For all r,n, Tot(φ)^n restricts to a morphism from the r-th source step to the r-th target step, whose composite with the target-step inclusion is the source-step inclusion followed by Tot(φ)^n. No vanishing assumptions are required.

source.place: Remark Tag 015K; the filtration formulas of homology.tex section-double-complex

proof.text: By Mathlib ιTotalOrZero_map, a source diagonal inclusion followed by the total map is its bidegree component followed by the corresponding target inclusion. That composite factors through the target image and through the target finite supremum because the index is in [r,n]. Pull back this target step along Tot(φ)^n. Each source inclusion factors through the pullback, so each source image lies in it. Finset.sup_le puts the source step in this pullback. Its universal property provides the desired map of steps and the commuting equation. Empty intervals are handled by the same supremum inequality.

lean.statement: theorem firstFiltration_map {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] (K L : HomologicalComplex₂ C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) [K.HasTotal (ComplexShape.up ℤ)] [L.HasTotal (ComplexShape.up ℤ)] (φ : K ⟶ L) (r n : ℤ) : ∃ f : ((K.firstFiltration n).step r : C) ⟶ ((L.firstFiltration n).step r : C), f ≫ ((L.firstFiltration n).step r).arrow = ((K.firstFiltration n).step r).arrow ≫ (total.map φ (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).f n
